name: Scales of Shale
description: Target creature gets +2/+0 and gains lifelink and indestructible until end of turn.
assumptions: Read node C's owner:"any" together with its "target" flag as an unrestricted "target creature" (any player's creature), not "target creature you control" — owner:any plus explicit targeting implies the controller isn't fixed by the node.
Treated node B (move, self, stack→gy) as ordinary post-resolution cleanup for an instant, not printed rules text, so it does not appear in the reconstructed description.
notes: Reconstruction of the given nodes was exact (mana cost {2}{B}, type Instant, and node C's cond:pt_delta=+2/+0;grant=lifelink_&_indestructible with lifetime:turn map 1:1 onto the real card's printed effect "Target creature gets +2/+0 and gains lifelink and indestructible until end of turn."). But the real card also carries `K:Affinity:Lizard` (Forge keyword line, forge-model/data/scales-of-shale.txt line 4) — Affinity for Lizards, reducing the cast cost by {1} for each Lizard the caster controls (Oracle line 1: "Affinity for Lizards (This spell costs {1} less to cast for each Lizard you control.)"). This entire mechanic is absent from the packet's nodes: there is no scaler node counting Lizards-you-control and no modifier/cost node tied to node A (the cast node) reducing its mana cost. This is a decomposition gap, not an agent error or schema gap — SCHEMA.md's `scaler` role and a cost-reduction `modifier`/`cond:` payload could express this (analogous to how `tap` nodes already express convoke-style alternate costs), the edge for it was simply never authored. For the forgeTranslate.ts bug-fixing pass: the `K:Affinity:Lizard` keyword line is not being translated into any edge/node at all — look at whichever function dispatches `K:` keyword lines into nodes and confirm it has no case for `Affinity` (Forge's generic cost-reduction-by-permanent-type keyword), unlike e.g. Convoke/Delve which apparently do get represented via `tap`/`source` nodes.
